address: Haarlemmerweg 518A-776, Amsterdam (north side of the Haarlemmerweg at the west end of the corridor): the 2023 residential block of 13 storeys with continuous white balcony slabs, glass balustrades and a glazed plinth
notes: Haarlemmerweg 518A-776 (BAG pand 0363100012250970, built 2023, 905 m2 footprint in one long block, eaves 41.7 m, 13 storeys, 137 addresses). NO MEASURABLE PHOTO: all-walls.ts finds one exposed wall (the 15.5 m east end); its only post-build crops are 2022-12-06 (TMX7316010203-002829_pano_0007_000166), which shows the building still scaffolded behind a green site hut and a Cloxam cabin, and 2025-07-01 (recording_2025-07-01_09-03-48_00810) at 88 m with 56 % tree cover. Both are declared unusable for measurement, so this recipe is INFERRED from what the 2025-07-01 crop does show: white balcony slab bands on every storey, glass balustrades on thin posts, a glazed wall behind with white mullions, and a glazed plinth with white columns.

No measured.json: no field here is a measurement. Every wall group lists its whole hand-held set in `hand`, and the colour, bay counts, storey splits and balcony frequency are read off the 2025 east crop only. Do not install on this evidence alone; a 2025+ panorama from the Haarlemmerweg front is what would settle it.

The other 17 street walls of the pand are party walls in 3DBAG (the row), so the block is drawn as four bearing groups: south (the Haarlemmerweg front), north (the rear), east end and west end. The plinth is glazed with the entrance on the south front.

Balcony bands are NOT drawn: on this shell the block-kit balcony row leaves parts on panels that do not host them (123 hostless parts, 160 m2 of openings outside their wall), because 3DBAG splits the 2023 block into 98 narrow planes. The 2025 crop shows glass-railed balcony bands on every storey, so this is a kit/shell gap, not a design choice: the plain wide-window grid is the honest stand-in until the shell or the balcony row is fixed.

Rendered 2026-10-21 (contact-aerial.png): most of the block still reads blank. Only the panels whose surfaces landed in a group with a workable width carry the window grid, and the four bearing groups cut across 98 small 3DBAG planes, so the big faces show as render with one band of windows near the top. The draft is a starting point for a shell/grouping pass, not a building.
